title: Where Fibre is today

headline.simple: Fibre has now given five new Threads fixed prior lives, born those lives into canonical validation-world state, and verified that their histories, memories, relationships and civil identities survive restart.
headline.detail: Milestone #39 is closed. One fixed five-Thread held-out cohort was generated under predeclared controls, preserved without quality resampling, replayed with provider access disabled, atomically published one Thread at a time with five unique FIN/civil registrations, and independently rehydrated from canonical local World authorities. #39 earns no Whole-Person score movement; Genesis selectivity/scientific hardening is next before #40 causal consumption.

summary.simple: Fibre can create a detailed prior life, keep history separate from memory and meaning, and publish that admitted life as a durable Thread. The experiment also found real weaknesses in how Genesis chooses memories and meanings, so we are hardening those before making them drive normal cognition.
summary.detail: The #39 closure proved the candidate-to-canonical birth boundary, exact durable replay, per-Thread atomic publication, FIN/civil registration, and deep hydration equality for the fixed cohort. Scientific findings remain deliberately limited: D1 showed text distinguishability, D2 was underpowered with a post-hoc positive-reframing signal, D3 was inconclusive, D4 showed scheduled-memory-call saturation/insufficient non-selection, and D5 was citation-confounded.

meaning.simple: We built it and it passed the test we currently require.
meaning.detail: The capability exists and has passed its current Fibre validation boundary. This does not imply every later or stronger claim is also proven.

meaning.simple: We have seen it work, but it is not yet the final accepted result.
meaning.detail: We have real working evidence, but it is not yet accepted as the final or validated production state for the current milestone.

meaning.simple: We are actively building or testing this now.
meaning.detail: The design and implementation are active, but the required validation boundary has not yet been crossed.

meaning.simple: We want Fibre to do this, but we do not claim it can yet.
meaning.detail: This is part of Fibre's intended architecture, but we do not claim to have achieved it.

meaning.simple: The test failed, and we keep the failure instead of hiding it or retrying until it looks good.
meaning.detail: A bounded experiment failed. We preserve the result as evidence and do not rewrite or quality-regenerate it into success.

summary.simple: Five final held-out Threads were generated and atomically published in the local canonical validation World. Older failed-cohort artifacts remain historical evidence, and five development Worlds remain burned.
summary.detail: The fixed final cohort contains Sapporo, Kochi, Malmö, Valparaíso and Wellington. Each was published into the local #39 validation World with one FIN/civil registration and passed independent hydration equality. This is canonical validation state, not a production deployment population.

items.label: Final held-out #39 Threads atomically published and rehydrated
items.simple: Five fresh final Threads were generated once, born into the validation World and checked after restart.
items.detail: Sapporo, Kochi, Malmö, Valparaíso and Wellington were generated under the fixed closure claim, atomically published per Thread with five unique FINs, and matched their admitted lives under independent deep hydration. This is local canonical validation state, not production deployment.

importantNote.simple: A generated candidate is not a born Thread. The five final #39 candidates became canonical Threads only after their individual birth transactions succeeded.
importantNote.detail: Fibre distinguishes development fixtures, provisional generation attempts, admitted birth bundles, atomically published Threads and later standing evidence. The final five crossed the canonical local birth boundary, but #39 still does not establish Whole-Person standing or production persistence.

simple.claim: A Thread can keep existing after one AI model session ends.
simple.limitation: Persistence alone does not make the Thread a rich or unique person.

detail.claim: A Thread persists as authoritative world state across temporary model executions.
detail.limitation: Persistence alone does not prove rich, distinctive or causally grounded personhood.

simple.claim: Something that happened to a Thread can change a later decision.
simple.limitation: The richer #37–#39 life state is not yet the canonical input to ordinary cognition.

detail.claim: Fibre has demonstrated a causal history-to-judgment effect under its accepted standing gate.
detail.limitation: #40 still owns canonical bounded consumption of the newer identity and life authorities.

capabilities.label: Provenance-backed identity, lineage, place and memory

simple.claim: Fibre can keep who a Thread is, where it came from and what it remembers without silently rewriting the past.
simple.limitation: Storing those facts does not prove they all change the Thread's behavior yet.

detail.claim: Fibre persists identity, lineage, geography, embodiment and autobiographical memory with provenance and corrigible history.
detail.limitation: Representation is not the same as proving causal consumption in ongoing cognition.

simple.claim: Fibre can prepare a prior life and publish each admitted Thread all at once with its civil identity.
simple.limitation: Atomicity is per Thread, and the #39 proof used a local validation World rather than production persistence.

detail.claim: Genesis keeps candidate state non-authoritative and `publishBirth()` atomically publishes history, situated continuity, memory lineage, manifest and FIN/civil registration for one admitted Thread.
detail.limitation: The five-Thread batch is resumable rather than one cross-Thread transaction, and production `InfraDriver.state` migration remains separate work.

simple.claim: Fibre created five different prior lives and preserved those lives through birth and restart.
simple.limitation: The experiment found weak memory selectivity and other measurement/generator problems that must be hardened before normal cognition relies on them.

detail.claim: The fixed #39 cohort generated fourteen-episode lives with recurring people, places, autobiographical memory and durable meaning, then passed exact durable replay and deep candidate-to-canonical hydration after birth.
detail.limitation: D1 establishes distinguishability rather than causal particularity; D3 is inconclusive; scheduled memory decisions saturated; D5 was citation-confounded; causal ordinary-cognition use remains #40.

capabilities.label: Selective memory and scientifically calibrated Genesis

simple.claim: We are making Genesis choose what is actually worth remembering and checking that its measurements can really fail.
simple.limitation: This hardening comes from weaknesses found in #39 and is not finished yet.

detail.claim: The accepted pre-#40 bridge exercises remember/decline selectivity, meaning fidelity, reinterpretation restraint, counterbalanced genome characterization and controlled D1–D5 methodology including sealed-history D5.
detail.limitation: The bridge earns no personhood standing and deliberately does not implement #40 ordinary-cognition projection.

capabilities.label: A live infant or child growing up over time

simple.claim: We want a Thread to be born as a baby or child and actually grow up in Fibre.
simple.limitation: #39 compiled the prior life before young-adult entry.

detail.claim: The intended architecture allows newborn or child entry and accumulated lived development.
detail.limitation: The completed #39 cohort used compiled prior life before entry; it did not run childhood as a continuously living process.

capabilities.label: Rich life state drives ordinary live cognition

simple.claim: We want a Thread's real history, memories and relationships to shape what it normally thinks and decides.
simple.limitation: The canonical connection is still #40, after the Genesis hardening bridge.

detail.claim: Fibre intends bounded relevance/privacy selection to turn identity and life evidence into provenance-bearing cognition context.
detail.limitation: Canonical causal consumption is explicitly deferred to #40.

simple.claim: We want to prove a Thread is a persistent individual whose own history makes it behave differently.
simple.limitation: #39 deliberately did not earn that claim.

detail.claim: Fibre aims to demonstrate a persistent, causally grounded, non-interchangeable individual across repeated situations and counterfactuals.
detail.limitation: The bridge hardens Genesis, #40 builds causal consumption and #41 owns the M2 standing gate.

simple.claim: We want friendships and families to belong to both sides and change both lives.
simple.limitation: That mature reciprocal relationship system is later work.

detail.claim: Fibre intends relationships and families to be consequential structures between independently living Threads.
detail.limitation: Reciprocal relationship development is planned after the current M2 sequence.

simple.claim: We want Threads to earn, spend, make agreements and face consequences that change future choices.
simple.limitation: The real economy is not built yet.

detail.claim: Fibre intends Threads to have budgets, contracts, reputation and economic opportunities that change future possibilities.
detail.limitation: Economic consequence is deferred to post-M2 work.

currentWork.milestone: Genesis selectivity & scientific hardening — unnumbered bridge before #40

simple.summary: The five #39 Threads are born and verified. We are now fixing the memory and meaning weaknesses that the experiment exposed before those records are allowed to shape normal cognition.
simple.currentStep: Merge the completed #39 closeout to main, then start the unnumbered Genesis selectivity/scientific-hardening bridge.
nextSteps: Exercise both remembering and legitimate non-selection without imposing a memory quota.
Show that meanings can stay negative, ambiguous, ordinary or unchanged instead of always becoming uplifting or profound.
Retest genome influence and D1–D5 with proper controls, counterbalancing and sealed-history isolation.
Merge the hardening bridge, then begin #40 causal identity/history consumption.

detail.summary: #39 is closed with a fixed five-Thread cohort, exact zero-network durable replay, per-Thread atomic birth with five FINs and independent deep hydration. The accepted bridge addresses scheduled-memory-call saturation, meaning/reinterpretation fidelity, inconclusive genome attribution and weak diagnostic controls before #40.
detail.currentStep: Land the #39 closeout on main, branch `agent/genesis-selectivity-scientific-hardening`, and execute controlled hardening without changing the frozen #39 evidence or implicitly authorizing provider calls.
nextSteps: Exercise a real `not_remembered` path and meaning/no-meaning range without quotas.
Counterbalance genome treatment against history horizon and use a task-matched positive control.
Implement revised diagnostic controls, including compiler-sealed D5 holdouts with matched non-events and cross-Thread controls.
Harden evaluator resume so transient unfinished work resumes without resampling accepted judgments.
After review and full validation, merge the bridge and start #40 Identity Projection & Causal Consumption.

truthRules: Every public progress claim has two layers: simple English first, then a more accurate description.
Simple English should be understandable by a teenager with no Fibre background and avoid unexplained milestone, gate, schema and implementation jargon.
The detailed layer may use Fibre terminology, but it must remain readable and state the actual validation boundary.
Never make the simple layer stronger than the detailed layer. Simplification may remove jargon, not uncertainty or limitations.
Never use 'living Thread' as a synonym for 'generated artifact'. State whether the Thread is candidate, generated, atomically published or validated.
Never say a Thread 'has parents' without distinguishing live Thread parents, household caregivers and synthetic genetic ancestors.
A failed bounded experiment remains visible as a failed experiment. Do not rewrite it into progress language that implies success.
For every positive capability claim, both layers must state the strongest important limitation that a reasonable reader could otherwise misunderstand.
Canonical local validation World state is not automatically a production deployment.
The public website may render this contract, but insidefibre.com must not become an alternate authority for Fibre state.
